description:
Divisions: Command and Control

Hi fellas. I've been an on-and-off Starsector player for years now and it's been my pleasure to enjoy the collective passion put into this game by both its developers and the many modders who have worked to enrich the Persean Sector with their creative vision. However, I've always lacked for technical skill, but now that gamma and seemingly beta cores have come online in real life, I now have the opportunity to - despite my deficiency in practical computer science knowledge - put in some things that I personally find to be very cool. This is my personal contribution to this game's ever expanding ecosystem of "cool things." It's a wonderful feeling to give something back, rather than just to consume the products of my betters.

Divisions: Command and Control is a combat AI overhaul that sets out to smooth some problems that I notice occur quite frequently in large battles - mainly that ships, both friend and foe, will end up tangling together in increasingly disadvantageous gunfights until they are destroyed with no regard for the wider situation of the battlefield. While the vanilla ship AI is very good at fighting in its localized space, it does not have the tactical finesse of something or someone that is led by command and control chain that is backed by training, experience, and decades of military history and doctrine. Certainly, the player is able to wrestle the AI into doing his or her bidding for their own fleet, but what of the enemy? Shouldn't the enemy fleet, too, not be capable of such things? And besides, shouldn't every fleet be able to more or less naturally synchronize in an autonomous fashion their capabilities at the lower and upper levels to great effect in order to achieve victory?

So the solution is simple. Divisions: Command and Control adds a Command and Control or C2 layer and duct-tapes it over the basic ship AI with the goal of making battles more interesting. The mod is not set out to "fix" anything per se but rather it is meant create emergent behavior mostly within fleet battles that ultimately leads to greater player engagement. With that being said, rigorous testing has yielded a consistent 90% winrate against vanilla AI of equivalent forces, so it likely makes many AI-controlled fleets a much greater challenge, but a mod of this kind is naturally rather difficult to test, so I will need your support and feedback.

The Command and Control chain is as follows:

The Player: The player has complete authority over his or her own fleet via the vanilla orders system.
The Officer in Tactical Command (OTC / Fleet Command): The OTC reads the whole battlefield, picks the operational phase (Approach, General Engagement, Coordinated Strike, Reinforce the Line, General Chase, or Fighting Retirement), maintains fleet-wide formations, designates the Main Effort and Reserve, and hands out orders to divisions. By default, this is you (or rather, your staff), or the commander of the largest ship deployed on the battlefield. You are free to pick whomever, but you will get massive command point penalties if your OTC is not actually deployed to the battlefield aboard a ship. The OTC performs his or her duties autonomously according to your Doctrine. You may override the OTC by interrupting its plans using the vanilla orders system.
Division Commanders: Division Commanders may lead divisions of up to 10 ships. They are responsible for managing their division formation, division-level tactics, coordination of missile and carrier strikes, and may take over OTC roles upon the destruction of their side's flagship. They may be overridden by you or the OTC.
The Ship: The individual ship follows its usual decision making as in vanilla. The basic ship AI may be overridden by its division commander, by the OTC at a more vague level, and by the player using vanilla means.

This applies to both player and NPC fleets. If you do not organize your own fleet into divisions, your ships will still use 100% vanilla AI (subject to your OTC), while NPC fleets will organize and fight according to their faction's doctrine.

Time, Space, and Firepower

Every ship and division projects three geometric domains on the battlefield (which you can toggle on and off in the Tab tactical map). The chain of command uses these domains to make decisions.

Time:

Time is a geometric descriptor of a ship or division's freedom of movement and ability to displace Space or Firepower within a 12-second window. Its base variable is Fleet-Point-weighted average speed, and it deforms inward along bearings where a division is pinned in contact or high on flux.

Space:

A geometric descriptor of a ship or division's zone of spatial control and ability to absorb pressure. Its base variable is weighted effective HP (hull, armor grid state, and shield/flux capacity). Overlapping friendly Space halos form strongpoints, and isolated friendly divisions inside enemy Space become weak points or seams.

Firepower:

Firepower is a 24-sector polar firepower rose combining alpha strike DPS, burst DPS, sustained flux-clamped DPS, and point defense arcs, padded by turret slew rates and hull turn rates over Time.

Convergence:

[REDACTED]

ACCESS GRANTED (Convergence)

Convergence meshes Time, Space, and Firepower together into a single non-linear phase-space product instead of adding them linearly. According to my beta core, multiplying the three domains together is mathematically superior to averaging them, and across 160 simulated 300 DP mirror battles it beat standard human C2 68.8% of the time.

Convergence decision-making (and the 4th overlay button on the tactical map) is only available to a fleet or division commanded by an installed Alpha Core (plus certain endgame non-human adversaries). If your flagship goes down or you have an Alpha Core commanding another ship in your fleet, it can hail you mid-battle to ask if it should assume tactical command.

The Officer in Tactical Command and your Division Commanders use these three domains to run down a hierarchical decision tree based on your Fleet Doctrine, fleet organization, and officer personalities. The goal of the entire script is simple: reduce the enemy's Time, Space, and Firepower to zero.

Campaign UI and Pre-Battle Deployment

Getting started with the mod is easy.

Step 1: Click on the Fleet Organization button in the Fleet window.

Step 2: Click on the auto-assign window to automatically create and assign your ships to divisions. Congratulations, you now have a solid C2 chain!

Step 3 (optional): Customize your fleet's doctrine down to division type, and the specific division.

Organization and Doctrine

Step 4 (optional): Engage in battle.

Requirements, Compatibility & Installation

Starsector Version: 0.98a-RC8
Dependencies: None required. LunaLib is optional and supported for in-game Mod Settings (chatter verbosity defaults to Minimal, overlay opacity, debug logging, and sector division reinitialization).
Save Compatibility: Safe to add to existing saves. Games saved before v1.0.3 cannot remove the mod safely. Update the mod and save again if you want to safely remove the mod.
Mod Compatibility: Built-in faction doctrine and nomenclature support for over 60 modded factions and should otherwise be able to handle any faction entity. Does not replace vanilla BasicShipAI, so it plays nicely with weapon/hullmods and combat plugins.

Other Features

Dynamic Music Engine: The mod introduces a system for dynamic battle music to play mid-battle based on your fleet's engagement level. This is mostly a proof of concept for now.
Deployment Points, max ships override: Accessible through the shift + F2 mod settings.

Installation:
1. Download the release archive and extract it into your Starsector/mods/ folder so that Starsector/mods/DivisionAI/mod_info.json exists.
2. Enable Divisions: Command and Control in the Starsector launcher.

Changelog
Detailed changes can be found on the GitHub repo.

v1.1.1d: Properly integrated pursuit battles with the mod.
v1.1.1c: Fixed MacOS and Linux compatibility issues. Send me logs if this isn't the case.
v1.1.0:
Improved UI clarity and added tooltips (slopped for now).
More aggressive behavior on Full Assault.
Improved obedience to player orders in general.
Fixed campaign fleet tooltip crash.
Improved helmsmanship and division cohesion.
Cross-mod campaign UI fixes with regards to the Fleet Organization and Fleet Doctrine buttons.
Added doctrinal and organizational options for ramming as a type of attack.
Stations as a concept are now properly understood as a concept for OTC and Division AI.

v1.0.5a: Division AI is now aware of ship skills and station keeping is improved.
v1.0.4d: Fixed tactical view extreme lag in some cases.
v1.0.4b: Fixed division circles UI bug with regards to player captaincy of his own ship.
v1.0.4: Fixed division circles UI bug.
v1.0.3: Fixed C2 taking over the the player's missile targeting choice and added compatibility for Arma Armatura's wingcom system.
v1.0.2: Codebase health and optimization.
v1.0.0: Initial release.

Mod Compatibility
Fully Compatible

All Faction Mods, Ship Packs & Weapon Packs: 100% compatible. 139 vanilla and modded factions (UAF, Iron Shell, Sindrian Fuel Co., Tahlan, Diable Avionics, Interstellar Imperium, HMI, Mayasura, SotF, AoTD, etc.) have built-in cultural division naming and fleet doctrines; any unlisted faction is dynamically profiled at runtime.[/url]
Nexerelin & Ashes of the Domain (AoTD): 100% compatible.
AI Tweaks: Compatible. Division AI steers ships via standard ShipwideAIFlags without replacing custom ShipAIPlugin or autofire plugins.
Second-in-Command / Officer Extension / Quality Captains: Compatible.
SpeedUp / Leading Pip / Detailed Combat Results / Combat Chatter: Compatible.

Compatible with Configuration / Notes

Arma Armatura (WingCom): Independent frigate-class Cataphracts work out of the box. For carrier-launched LPC wings using WingCom officers or player neural-transfer, set that carrier division's Voidstrike Coordination to Uncoordinated and Target Observance to Free (or keep the carrier in Unassigned Ships) so Voidstrike Stage 1 marshalling does not tether WingCom fighters. (Automatic WingCom detection planned for a future update.)[/url]
RTS Assist: Ships inside an active Division will try to hold their division formation slot over RTS Assist move vectors.

Incompatible (Overlapping UI Hooks)

Pre-Battle Deployment Orders / CustomDeployment: Both mods overhaul the vanilla pre-battle Deployment Dialog layout and initial wave placement. Do not enable alongside this mod.
